purpose: Correct the source-class overstatement in v7.6 and classify the entire three-C4 smooth Hamiltonian C12 class at the orbit-relation level. The v7.6 saturated EQ_3 graph is a valid simple 4-regular Hamiltonian graph with three complementary C4s, but its X and Z inner C4s are selfcrossing relative to the displayed Hamiltonian order, so it is not a smooth/non-selfcrossing control for the Fleischner--Sabidussi hard source. Exhaustive smooth enumeration finds no saturated EQ_3 or NEQ_3 triangle, while still exposing exact nontrivial twisted bijections.

source_fact.reference: H. Fleischner and G. Sabidussi, 3-colorability of 4-regular hamiltonian graphs, Journal of Graph Theory 42(2) (2003), 125-140, DOI 10.1002/jgt.10079.
source_fact.hard_class: The NP-complete source requires the complementary cycles of the supplied Hamiltonian cycle to be non-selfcrossing cycles of constant length at least four.
source_fact.smooth_C4_port_test: For a labelled complementary C4 with cyclic ports 0,1,2,3, its four occurrences along the Hamiltonian cycle must appear in a dihedral cyclic order: a rotation of 0,1,2,3 or a rotation of 0,3,2,1.

v7_6_correction.corrected_scope: The v7.6 EQ_3 control remains a valid fully saturated three-C4 Hamiltonian control in the broader class, but it is not a smooth/non-selfcrossing hard-source control. Every v7.6 sentence calling this particular EQ graph smooth is superseded by v7.6.1. The relaxed NEQ cycle and the reusable-three-cycle negative gate are not invalidated by this correction.

complete_smooth_three_C4_enumeration.canonical_generation: Rotate the Hamiltonian C12 so the first symbol is component 0. Enumerate cyclic words over {0,1,2} with multiplicity four each and no equal adjacent symbols, including the last-first pair. Give each component ports 0,1,2,3 in its occurrence order; this constructs exactly the smooth/non-selfcrossing three-C4 source representations, with harmless duplicate cyclic representations allowed.

exact_bijective_relations.meaning: Smooth triangle holonomy can transmit one full three-state orbit variable through a nontrivial permutation, but it does not realize identity EQ_3 or the D4 port-swap permutation [0,2,1] in a fully saturated three-C4 C12.

explicit_smooth_twisted_wire_control.meaning: This is a genuine smooth fully saturated C12 example whose exact two-terminal orbit relation is a bijection. It is a closed control, not yet a reusable reduction wire because every Hamiltonian port is saturated.

open_port_twisted_control.scope: The internal edge set is structurally source-completable because it is a subgraph of the displayed smooth Hamiltonian C12 word. This does not prove relation-preserving external completion. In particular one named terminal has only one free Hamiltonian half-edge, so it does not contradict the v7.6 exhaustive reusable-wire gate requiring at least two free half-edges on each terminal.

positive: Restores the source firewall: the hard smooth/non-selfcrossing class must be preserved explicitly in every future gadget claim.
Shows cycle holonomy remains genuinely expressive even inside the true smooth class: exact three-state twisted bijections occur.
Provides a concrete open-port asymmetric twisted relation that can seed four-plus-component splicing searches.
killed_or_corrected: Using the v7.6 saturated EQ_3 example as evidence that smooth three-C4 C12 already realizes EQ_3.
Assuming Hamiltonian plus disjoint C4 complement automatically implies smooth/non-selfcrossing.
Assuming the first smooth cyclic relation must be EQ_3 or NEQ_3 rather than a twisted permutation.
firewall: The exhaustive 268-word statement is only for fully saturated smooth Hamiltonian C12 with exactly three complementary C4 components.
The nine-edge open-port relation is not yet a compositional source wire; relation-preserving completion and splicing remain open.

next_target.directive: Preserve non-selfcrossing inner-cycle order as a mandatory source invariant. Starting from the exact smooth twisted permutations above, search four-or-more C4 Hamiltonian gadgets whose hidden components are fully saturated and whose two named terminals retain at least two controlled external half-edges each. Track full S3 gain sets, orbit permutation transport, port usage, and Hamiltonian-word splicing. A success must include a relation-preserving splice lemma; a negative result must distinguish failure caused by smooth order from failure caused only by port capacity.
